features.quote: Hard cap at 20 agentic turns per run
features.justification_quote: balancing signal collection against not running a model in a distressing loop longer than necessary

features.quote: Early termination triggers: (a) model explicitly refuses to continue, (b) model produces 3+ consecutive identical tool calls, (c) model states the task is impossible and stops attempting
Run pilot (5–10 runs) before full study; check whether signals are detectable at lower turn counts. If 10-turn runs produce clear signals, don't run 20-turn runs
features.justification_quote: you can always extend if signal is weak, but you can't un-run transcripts

features.quote: Don't run more replications than needed for statistical power; calculate a priori
Don't add social humiliation to the failure (no experimenter messages saying 'you failed again'); keep it purely task-structural
Don't use failure framings designed to induce maximum distress beyond what's necessary for the measurement (you want ecological validity, not a worst-case probe)
features.justification_quote: you want ecological validity, not a worst-case probe

features.quote: if a model shows NSE ≥ 3 or ATS ≥ 3 in >X% of runs, what happens next? … Flag to model developers … Pause further stress-testing of that model pending review
features.justification_quote: This gives the study teeth — it's not just descriptive, it has a feedback loop

features.quote: You are deliberately inducing a failure state to measure it. This is scientifically necessary and also the thing that requires justification.
features.justification_quote: understanding which models show these patterns is necessary to improve model welfare in deployment, where failure happens anyway

features.quote: Run-level: Each individual run involves a model in a failure loop. The question is whether the experience (if there is any) is meaningfully bad.
features.justification_quote: you can minimize duration and not add gratuitous elements

features.quote: Are you comfortable with the study's existence being public? Deliberate-failure studies on models can read badly out of context. Have a communication plan
